fact_en:
Ever wonder where puddles go on hot days?

Liquid water absorbs heat energy and transforms into invisible water vapor in the air!
fact_bis:
Naa ba ka nahibalo kung asa mawala ang mga latian sa init nga adlaw?

Ang liquid water mo-absorb og heat energy ug mo-transform ngadto sa invisible water vapor sa hangin!

findings.note: EN hook "where puddles go on hot days" became "asa mawala ang mga latian" — latian = swamp/marshland, a different thing from a puddle (Cebuano lunang/danaw). A swamp does not evaporate away on a hot day, and the card never mentions puddles again, so the observation the card is built on is lost.

fact_en: The Mindoro tamaraw wallows in muddy soil and freshwater pools to cool its body down during the hot, dry summer season!
fact_bis: Ang Mindoro tamaraw mokalingkawas sa lapok nga yuta ug freshwater pools aron mapabugnaw ang lawas niya sa init nga ting-init!

findings.note: EN "The Mindoro tamaraw wallows in muddy soil and freshwater pools to cool its body" became "mokalingkawas sa lapok nga yuta" = ESCAPES/frees itself FROM the muddy soil. That reverses the relationship (it goes INTO the mud, Cebuano molunang/maglunang) and contradicts the cooling reason the card gives. Nothing else in the card restores it.

fact_en: Continual radioactive decay of isotopes inside Earth provides heat! This heat drives the motion of the mantle and the tectonic plates.
fact_bis: Ang padayon nga radioactive decay sa mga isotope sulod sa Earth naghatag ug kainit! Kining kainita ang nagpalihok sa mantle ug sa mga tectonic plate.

findings.note: title_bis "Pagkadunot sa Radyo" = "decay/rotting of the RADIO (the appliance)". Radioactive is radyoaktibo, never radyo, and the card's own body and emph_bis keep the correct term "radioactive decay" — classic title-outlier. The title alone names a different thing (a broken radio) as the source of Earth's internal heat.

fact_en:
Why do you feel dizzy during a heatwave?

Your body sweats to cool down! But losing too much water makes your brain feel dizzy and confused.
fact_bis:
Nganong nahihilo ug nalibog ka panahon sa heatwave?

Nagapawis ang lawas aron mobugnaw! Pero kung sobra ang mawala nga tubig, mahimong mahilo ug malibog ang imong utok.

findings.note: EN "feel dizzy" is rendered with Tagalog hilo (and Tagalog morphology "nahihilo"). In Cebuano hilo = POISON; dizzy is lipong/lipong-lipong. Question reads "Nganong nahihilo... ka panahon sa heatwave?" and the body repeats it: "mahimong mahilo ug malibog ang imong utok" = your brain gets POISONED and confused. Nothing in the card restores "dizzy" (the title only carries libog = confused), so a Cebuano-only reader learns that dehydration poisons the brain — a different, false claim. This is the confirmed hilo false friend.

fact_en: Astronauts on the International Space Station lose bone density because in microgravity, their skeleton no longer supports their body weight!
fact_bis: Sa microgravity sa International Space Station, ang mga astronaut makasinati og bone density loss kay ang ilang skeleton dili na mag-support sa ilang lawas!

findings.note: title_bis "Buto sa Kawanangan" for "Bones in Space". Tagalog false friend: Cebuano bone is BUKOG; "buto" in Cebuano is an explosion/burst (and vulgar slang for genitals), never bone. Nothing in the card corrects it - the body carries the fact only in English ("bone density loss", "skeleton") and never says bukog once, so a child reading only the Cebuano gets no Cebuano word for the thing the card is about. Compare ffct-35715 in this same batch, which titles bones correctly as "Kalsiyo sa Bukog".

fact_en:
Did you know soil has layers like a cake?

Soil has layers called horizons! The topsoil is the richest layer because it holds the most humus from decayed plants and animals.
fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang yuta adunay mga layer sama sa cake?

Ang yuta adunay mga layer nga gitawag ug horizons, ug ang topsoil mao ang pinakabug-at nga layer kay puno kini ug humus gikan sa mga nabuak nga tanom ug hayop.

findings.note: Body: "ang topsoil mao ang pinakabug-at nga layer" = "topsoil is the HEAVIEST layer" (EN: the RICHEST layer). Bug-at is weight, not nutrient richness, so a child ends up believing a false claim about soil horizons (topsoil is in fact the lightest, most organic layer). Same card also has "humus gikan sa mga NABUAK nga tanom ug hayop" - nabuak = broken/shattered, not decayed (madunot) - the confirmed mabuak/madunot seam. Sister card ffct-35733 in this batch states the fact correctly: "ang topsoil ang nag-gunit sa pinakadaghan nga organic matter".

fact_en: Fishermen in coastal towns like Roxas City use the moon's gravity to predict when tides will be high or low!
fact_bis: Gigamit sa mga mangingisda sa mga baybayon sama sa Roxas City ang grabidad sa bulan aron ma-predict ang taas ug ubos nga balod!

findings.note: Body: "ang grabidad sa bulan aron ma-predict ang taas ug ubos nga BALOD" = "to predict high and low WAVES". Balod is a wind-driven wave; tide is taob (high) / hunas (low). As written the card teaches that the moon's gravity controls how big the waves are, which is false science, and nothing in the Cebuano restores it (title_bis keeps the English word "Tides"). Other cards in this same batch use the correct term - ffct-35705 "Taob sa Dagat", ffct-35844 "Taob ug Sakit", ffct-35826 "Sulog sa Bulan".

fact_en: Halite is the mineral name for rock salt! It naturally forms perfect cubic crystals when the water around it evaporates.
fact_bis: Ang halite mao ang mineral name para sa rock salt! Natural kining maghimo og perpektong cubic crystals kung ma-evaporate ang tubig niini.

findings.note: title_bis "Halite nga Kubyeta" for "Halite Cube Crystals". "Kubyeta/kubeta" means TOILET (latrine) in Cebuano and Tagalog, not cube - the title reads "Halite the toilet". The card's own body uses the correct idea in English ("perpektong cubic crystals"), which is exactly the title-outlier signature; the Cebuano title names a completely different object and is never repaired in Cebuano.

fact_en: Talc is the softest mineral on the standard hardness scale, and it is actively mined in the municipality of Masinloc, Zambales!
fact_bis: Ang Talc mao ang pinakaluag nga mineral sa standard hardness scale, ug kini actively mined sa munisipyo sa Masinloc, Zambales!

findings.note: "Talc is the SOFTEST mineral on the hardness scale" -> "Ang Talc mao ang PINAKALUAG nga mineral sa standard hardness scale". Cebuano luag = loose/slack/roomy (luag nga sapatos), not soft; soft is humok. The whole point of the card is the hardness ranking, and nothing else in the card restores it — a child reads "the loosest mineral on the hardness scale", which is meaningless, so the fact that talc is the softest mineral is gone.

fact_en: Typhoon floodwaters hide harmful bacteria! If you rub your eyes with dirty hands after playing in the flood, it can cause severe eye infections.
fact_bis: Ang baha gikan sa bagyo adunay nakatago nga harmful bacteria! Kung hagkon nimo ang imong mata gamit ang hugaw nga kamot, makapahinabo kini og grabe nga eye infections.

findings.note: "If you RUB your eyes with dirty hands" -> "Kung HAGKON nimo ang imong mata gamit ang hugaw nga kamot". Cebuano hagkon = to KISS (halok); rub the eyes is kuskuson/kusi-kusihon. Wrong-sense verb in a safety card: the hazardous action itself becomes an impossible one (kissing your own eye with your hand), and the card never states the real behaviour to avoid, so the hand-to-eye transmission warning is not recoverable from the Cebuano.

fact_en:
Why should you always wear gloves when handling compost or potting soil?

Animal feces in the dirt can transmit harmful parasitic worms to humans, so always wear gloves!
fact_bis:
Ngano nga kanunay ka mag-gloves kung mag-handle ka og compost o potting soil?

Ang ihi-iho sa hayop sa yuta makadala og harmful parasitic worms sa tawo, mao nga kanunay mag-gloves!

findings.note: bis body says "Ang ihi-iho sa hayop sa yuta makadala og harmful parasitic worms" for EN "Animal feces in the dirt can transmit harmful parasitic worms". Cebuano `ihi` = URINE (mangihi = to urinate); feces is `tae`/`iti`. The card names a different substance as the parasite vector and never corrects it — a Cebuano-only reader learns that animal urine in soil carries parasitic worms, which is false, and this is a health/safety card.

fact_en: Traditional bahay kubo houses are built on stilts with lightweight materials to minimize damage from natural hazards like earthquakes and floods!
fact_bis: Ang tradisyonal nga bahay kubo gitukod sa stilts gamit ang lightweight nga materyales aron mapaminusan ang kadaut gikan sa natural hazards sama sa linog ug baha!

findings.note: title_bis "Bahay Kubo Sulo" for "Stilted Bahay Kubo". Cebuano `sulo` = TORCH (also Tagalog); it has no stilt/post sense — stilts is `tukod` (or haligi/poste). The title tells a Cebuano-only reader the card is about a torch, and the card's own body keeps the correct concept only in English ("gitukod sa stilts"), so the headline fact — the house stands on raised posts, which is WHY it survives quakes and floods — never appears in Cebuano anywhere on the card.
